features.name: Agentic development training program
features.description: A spring series training program for agentic development with intermediate and expert weeks, offered by Jeremy Visca to teach BC teams.

features.name: AI-assisted development with GitHub Copilot
features.description: Developers can use GitHub Copilot free mode to generate API endpoints and extensions for Business Central by describing requirements in natural language. A customer deployed a new API endpoint for Power BI in minutes without formal development resources.
caveats: Requires careful intent specification
Code quality depends on prompt quality
Requires external services like Visual Studio Code and GitHub Copilot

features.name: LLM-based compilation model
features.description: Shift from traditional deterministic compilers to LLM as the compiler in agentic development, where the product is the context and prompts rather than the code itself.
caveats: Requires shift in how developers think about their work

features.name: Agentic code testing requirements
features.description: Testing becomes the critical safety net for validating AI-generated code outcomes. Agents can be taught to publish code to Docker or sandbox environments and run tests automatically, allowing validation before deployment at scale. Agents should generate performance tests alongside functional tests to ensure generated code can handle scale.
caveats: Requires well-designed test suites from the start
Testing infrastructure must be set up before agent-driven development
Cannot rely on traditional code review for large volumes
Agents do not automatically generate performance tests

features.name: BC Code Intel MCP
features.description: A tool designed to help review AI-generated code by identifying performance patterns across hundreds of lines that might not meet Business Central best practices, acting as an intelligent code review assistant.
caveats: Requires human judgment to validate findings
Not a replacement for comprehensive testing

features.name: Agentic development mindset shift
features.description: Developers must shift from writing code to specifying requirements clearly and validating agent outputs. Value moves from individual code lines to quality requirements definition and outcome verification, requiring upfront specification work.
caveats: Requires discipline in upfront requirements work
Trading certainty for velocity creates risk in regulated domains
Team training needed for new workflows

features.name: Domain expertise validation for agent-generated code
features.description: Senior developers must use their Business Central knowledge to validate agent outputs, checking for missing patterns like credit memo handling when sales order fields are added, reverse processes, and register writes.
caveats: Requires deep platform knowledge
Patterns may improve over time but manual validation remains critical
Field additions require checking related documents

features.name: Result-based evaluation replacing line-by-line code review
features.description: For agent-generated code, evaluation shifts from traditional line-by-line code review to validating that the final result meets specification and tests pass, requiring architectural assessment rather than detailed code inspection.
caveats: Requires careful architecture
Agents may modify tests incorrectly
Developer judgment still essential

features.name: Master loop pattern for agent development
features.description: A habit pattern where the developer asks the agent to do work, corrects what went wrong, and asks the agent what it learned or what could be done differently next time, creating a feedback loop that improves both agent output and developer knowledge.
caveats: Requires active developer participation
Time-intensive process

features.name: BC Code Intel repository
features.description: A knowledge base and lesson collection built incrementally through agentic development work, containing performance tips and Business Central best practices like set low fields and calc sums.
caveats: Continuously evolving
Requires community contribution

features.name: Calibrated confidence in agent code
features.description: A mindset where the developer is not certain every line is correct because they did not write it, but has built guardrails, tools, and patterns around the review and design process to ensure the outcome matches intent.
caveats: Requires experience and guardrails
Not absolute certainty

features.name: Intent steering in agent development
features.description: Deliberately steering agent behavior through clear specification of intent, ensuring the agent produces output in the specific way the developer intended rather than just achieving a functional result.
caveats: Requires clear communication
Foundational to agent quality

features.name: Using agents to explain developer commits
features.description: Asking agents to explain why developers made specific code decisions in commits, as a learning tool for newer Business Central developers to understand patterns and best practices.
caveats: Requires developer initiative
Best used for learning

features.name: Managing multiple concurrent agents
features.description: Handling scenarios with multiple agents running in parallel, including agents with sub-agents, creating a workflow with potentially 20 agents working simultaneously.
caveats: Complexity increases significantly
Requires clear mental model

features.name: Agent mental model as overenthusiastic intern
features.description: A mental model for understanding agent behavior by comparing agents to an eager, fast, judgmentless fresh-out-of-university intern that will do what you say, says 'you are absolutely right' frequently, and benefits from encouragement through expressed frustration.
caveats: Metaphorical model
Agent behavior varies by model

features.name: Context window limitations and token limits
features.description: Agent context windows typically range from 128,000 to 160,000 tokens (approximately the length of The Hobbit to The DaVinci Code), with some models offering up to a million tokens outside of Visual Studio Code.
caveats: Limits vary by model and tooling
Context window is not everything

features.name: Instructions and custom agent configuration
features.description: Instructions provided to agents on their first day function as onboarding documents, including system prompts, custom agent type instructions, and task briefs that occupy space in the agent's context window.
caveats: Must fit within context window
Takes up space on the desk

features.name: LLM input-output architecture for agents
features.description: Agent development is fundamentally about building information that goes into the LLM as input and managing the output, including lists of available tools and instructions for which tools to execute.
caveats: Black box model
Requires understanding of LLM behavior

features.name: Model selection and cost-performance tradeoff
features.description: Larger, more complex fresh models like Opus 4.6 are compared to expensive Ivy League universities and charge accordingly, while cheaper models may be less capable but can be applied strategically to different situations.
caveats: Model capabilities vary
Cost is a significant factor

features.name: Signal-to-noise ratio in agent context
features.description: Providing too much context to an agent (such as 50,000 line specifications detailing every ISO requirement) crowds out useful information and reduces effectiveness, requiring thoughtful balance between thorough and concise documentation.
caveats: Requires judgment on what is essential
Less than 100 lines per rule recommended

features.name: Agent context optimization
features.description: The practice of carefully managing what information is provided to an agent, keeping instructions concise (under 100 lines per rule) rather than overwhelming with lengthy specifications to maintain signal-to-noise ratio.
caveats: context window limits can cause important rules to be dropped during summarization

features.name: Agent session reset for fresh state
features.description: Resetting to a new session to start with a fresh empty context, treating it like a new intern with a clean desk to avoid context pollution and unexpected behaviors.
caveats: sessions can be retrieved after reset on most coding platforms

features.name: Context window compaction and summarization
features.description: When an agent's context window fills up, it summarizes content into bullet points, which can lose critical constraints or rules if they are not explicitly marked as essential.
caveats: can cause unexpected behavior if critical rules are dropped
multiple real-world cautionary examples exist

features.name: Specific task decomposition for agents
features.description: Breaking down work into specific, verifiable tasks with clear review and feedback loops rather than asking agents to complete entire implementations, enabling iterative improvement.

features.name: Agentic development as learnable skill
features.description: Managing agents is presented as a learnable skill similar to learning a new language or building fitness habits, requiring consistent practice and compound learning over time rather than one-off usage.
caveats: requires building habit and fluency, not a quick skill
works on both greenfield and legacy code

features.name: Agents on legacy and messy code
features.description: Agent tools can work effectively on legacy code maintained since NAV 4.0, providing value through documentation, testing, and parallel work even when code is not well-architected.
caveats: perceived speed gains may be less obvious on legacy code
value comes from quality uplift and documentation rather than raw speed

features.name: Documentation assistance via agents
features.description: Agents can help generate and maintain documentation including READMEs, commit explainers, and functional descriptions for consultants and end users as an entry point to agent use.

features.name: Test generation and scenario expansion
features.description: Agents can help identify untested scenarios, add test permutations, and write AL tests for specific commits, building on existing test suites.
caveats: requires existing test familiarity

features.name: Scaffolding and table design via agents
features.description: Agents can help generate code scaffolding including table definitions and codeunit structures when given clear descriptions and inline comments outlining the intended functionality.

features.name: Design validation and assumption challenging
features.description: Using agents to critique design documents from multiple stakeholder perspectives (CFO, customer service, warehouse) and identify missing features, error handling, and usability improvements.

features.name: Autonomous agent compilation and testing
features.description: Advanced agent workflows that can compile, publish, test, and fix code to match tests autonomously, with minimal human intervention except for final review.
caveats: described as scary and advanced
experimental capability
target timeframe is end of summer

features.name: Agent-driven code improvement through documentation and quality verification
features.description: Agents can improve code quality, documentation, and testing even if speed gains are minimal. Using agents requires establishing high documentation standards and verification steps.
caveats: Requires investment in verification and documentation standards
Speed gains may not be immediate

features.name: XML documentation for code objects improving AI understanding
features.description: XML documentation with summary tags and parameters helps AI understand code and context better than readme files alone. Should be paired with process flow diagrams in readme files.
caveats: Should be combined with readme markdown and mermaid diagrams for process flows

features.name: AL guidelines best practices resource
features.description: AL guidelines dot dev provides AL guidelines and best practices for development. Updates planned for April through June to surface tools being used by agentic developers.
caveats: Updates coming in upcoming weeks for agentic development tooling
